q: Was Pleasant Home (217 Home Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: Pleasant Home, the John Farson House, was designed by Prairie School architect George W. Maher and completed in 1897.

q: Was Cheney Mansion (220 N Euclid Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: Cheney Mansion was designed in 1913 by Charles E. White Jr., a student of Wright. It is not a Wright building.

q: Was the Edwin H. Cheney House (520 N East Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: Yes. Don't mix it up with Cheney Mansion: Wright designed the 1903 Cheney House for Mamah Borthwick and Edwin Cheney.

q: Was Scoville Square (119-137 N Oak Park Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: Scoville Square, originally the Masonic Temple Building (1906-09), was designed by Eben Ezra Roberts.

q: Was the Charles E. Matthews House (432 N Kenilworth Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: It is a 1909 Prairie School house by Tallmadge & Watson, per the Village of Oak Park landmarks list.

q: Was the Vernon W. Skiff House (633 N East Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: It is a 1909 Prairie School house by Nimmons & Fellows. Wright's William E. Martin House is across the street at 636.

q: Was the Arthur Heurtley House (318 Forest Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: Yes. Wright designed it in 1902 for banker Arthur Heurtley and his wife Grace.

q: Was the Chester Flitcraft House (845 Chicago Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: It is a c. 1914 Prairie School house by John S. Van Bergen, one block east of the Wright Home and Studio on Chicago Ave.

q: Was the Edward and Caroline McCready House (231 N Euclid Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: It is a 1907 Prairie School house by Spencer and Powers. Wright's George Furbeck House is on the same block at 223.

q: Was the Oscar B. Balch House (611 N Kenilworth Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: Yes. Wright designed it in 1911 for decorator Oscar B. Balch.

q: Was the Ernest Hemingway Birthplace (339 N Oak Park Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: The 1890 Queen Anne house was designed by Wesley A. Arnold, according to the Village landmarks list.

q: Was the First Methodist Episcopal Church (324 N Oak Park Ave) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: The 1923 Gothic Revival church was designed by Tallmadge & Watson.

q: Was Oak Park Village Hall (123 Madison St) designed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
explain: The Modernist Village Hall was designed by Harry Weese and built in 1975.

q: Which Oak Park building by Frank Lloyd Wright is part of a UNESCO World Heritage inscription?
explain: Unity Temple (1905-08) is one of eight Wright sites in "The 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright" inscription.

q: What material forms the exterior of Unity Temple, left uncovered by plaster, brick, or stone?
explain: Wright built Unity Temple as a monolithic cube of concrete and left the concrete exposed.

q: In what year did Frank Lloyd Wright build his Oak Park home?
explain: Wright built his home in 1889 and added the Studio along Chicago Avenue in 1897.

q: The Home and Studio has been restored to how it looked in which year?
explain: The Frank Lloyd Wright Trust restored the Home and Studio to its 1909 appearance between 1974 and 1987.

q: Which Oak Park house did Wright call the 'progenitor of Fallingwater'?
explain: Its cantilevered balconies and roofs led Wright to call the 1909 Laura Gale House the progenitor of Fallingwater.

q: Which house was the first of Wright's mature Prairie-style homes built in Oak Park?
explain: The Frank W. Thomas House (1901) was the first mature Prairie-style residence by Wright in Oak Park.

q: The Nathan G. Moore House was rebuilt after a fire. Who redesigned its upper stories in 1923?
explain: Fire destroyed the second and third stories in 1922, and Wright redesigned them in 1923.

q: Wright designed the Thomas Gale House on his own while working for which firm? These are his 'bootleg' houses.
explain: The Thomas and Laura Gale House is one of the 'bootleg' designs Wright made independently while employed by Adler and Sullivan.

q: What shape are the two turrets beside the entrance of the George Furbeck House?
explain: Two large octagonal turrets flank the entrance, which leads to an octagonal living room.

q: Wright and sculptor Richard Bock designed a fountain that now stands as a replica in which park?
explain: The original Scoville Park (Horse Show) Fountain deteriorated and was demolished; a replica was installed in 1969.

q: What happened to the Hills-DeCaro House during a 1976 restoration?
choices: It was moved to River Forest
Its roof was replaced with glass
A fire burned much of it
explain: The house caught fire during a 1976 restoration and much of the first floor burned; it was later rebuilt.

q: On what date was Ernest Hemingway born at 339 N Oak Park Ave?
explain: Hemingway was born July 21, 1899, in the Queen Anne home of his grandparents Ernest and Caroline Hall.

q: Which architect designed the Hemingway family's 1906 home at 600 N Kenilworth Ave?
explain: Henry Fiddelke designed it in 1906 for Dr. Clarence and Grace Hemingway. Ernest lived there from 1906 to 1918.

q: Which park was the first parcel of land bought by the Park District of Oak Park?
explain: Scoville Park was bought in 1912 and was the first parcel the Park District acquired.

q: What is the focal point of Scoville Park?
explain: The World War I 'Peace Triumphant' Monument was unveiled on November 11, 1925.

q: Whose memorial bust stands near the War Memorial in Scoville Park?
explain: The Percy Julian Memorial Bust was unveiled in 2003 to honor the chemist and longtime Oak Park resident.

q: Which park is home to the hand-operated 'Rehm Park Trains'?
explain: Free hand-operated trains run on a track inside the Rehm Park playground, which was originally called 'South Park.'

q: Which park is sometimes called 'The Secret Garden'?
explain: Austin Gardens sits in a quiet neighborhood just north of Lake Street.

q: Taylor Park was originally called what?
explain: Taylor Park was first called North Park and was renamed for Henry A. Taylor, first president of the Park Board.

q: Field Park is named after which children's author?
explain: The park was acquired in 1916 and named for children's author Eugene Field.

q: Which famous landscape architect originally designed Scoville, Rehm, and Taylor parks?
explain: Park District histories credit Jens Jensen with the original designs of Scoville, Rehm, and Taylor parks.

q: Mills Park is named after Herbert S. Mills. Whom did he buy the property from in 1910?
explain: Herbert S. Mills bought it from John Farson's widow in 1910. The Park District acquired it in 1939.

q: In what year was the Oak Park Conservatory built?
explain: The Conservatory at 615 Garfield St was built in 1929 by Foley Greenhouse Manufacturing.

q: Before it was renamed for chemist Percy Julian, what was Julian Middle School called?
explain: Percy Julian Middle School used to be Nathaniel Hawthorne Middle School.

q: Oak Park's early settlers Joseph and Betty Kettlestrings emigrated from where?
explain: The Kettlestrings, immigrants from Yorkshire, England, staked out a farm in 1835. Locals once called the area Kettlestrings Grove.

q: In what year did the Village of Oak Park pass a fair housing ordinance?
explain: Oak Park passed a fair housing ordinance in 1968.

q: On what date did the current Oak Park Main Library open to the public?
explain: The Main Library at 834 Lake Street opened on October 5, 2003.

q: Ray Kroc was born in Oak Park in 1902. Which company did he build into a global giant?
explain: Ray Kroc was born in Oak Park on Oct. 5, 1902, and built McDonald's into a worldwide fast-food chain.

q: Which 'Golden Girls' star was born at Oak Park's West Suburban Hospital in 1922?
explain: Betty White was born Jan. 17, 1922, at West Suburban Hospital in Oak Park. Her family moved to Los Angeles when she was a toddler.

q: Oak Park-born author Carol Shields won a Pulitzer Prize for which novel?
explain: Carol Shields, born in Oak Park in 1935, won the Pulitzer Prize for The Stone Diaries. She moved to Canada in 1957.

q: Doris Humphrey, born in Oak Park in 1895, became a pioneer of what art form?
explain: Doris Humphrey, born in Oak Park on Oct. 17, 1895, was a pioneer of 20th-century modern dance, known for 'fall and recovery.'

q: Edgar Rice Burroughs lived at 414 Augusta St. from 1914 to 1917. Which famous character did he create?
explain: Tarzan author Edgar Rice Burroughs lived at 414 Augusta St. from 1914 to 1917 and wrote more Tarzan books there.

q: After graduating from Oak Park's high school in 1917, Ernest Hemingway became a reporter for which newspaper?
explain: Hemingway graduated from OPRF in 1917 and went to report for The Kansas City Star.

q: Before comedy stardom, Oak Park-born Bob Newhart worked by day in Chicago as what?
explain: Bob Newhart was born in Oak Park in 1929. He worked as an accountant in Chicago by day and did comedy by night before making it big.

q: Chemist Percy Julian moved to Oak Park in 1950. He made useful medical compounds from which plant?
explain: Dr. Percy Julian made compounds from soybeans to treat arthritis, glaucoma and allergies. He held more than 130 patents.

q: In 1902 Oak Park became its own village by separating from which township?
explain: Oak Park was incorporated as a village on Jan. 25, 1902, and separated from Cicero Township.

q: The settlement was first called Kettlestrings Grove. What was its next name, before Oak Park?
explain: The area was first called Kettlestrings Grove and then Oak Ridge, after a ridge of dry land full of oak trees. Later it became Oak Park.

q: Oak Park was 'dry' for nearly a century. When liquor sales began in 1973, who got the first liquor license?
explain: Oak Park approved liquor sales in 1973. The first license went to Ascension Catholic Church for its social events.

q: In 1976 Oak Park won which national honor?
explain: Oak Park was named an All-America City in 1976.

q: In 1932, Oak Park voters approved something that had not been allowed before. What was it?
explain: In 1932, a local vote approved showing movies on Sundays in Oak Park.

q: In Oak Park's government, which top official is appointed rather than elected?
explain: Voters elect the Village President, six Trustees and the Village Clerk. The Village Manager is appointed.

q: Which station is the western end of the CTA Green Line, at Oak Park's western edge?
explain: Harlem/Lake is the Green Line's western terminal. It sits next to Metra's Oak Park station.

q: Which Metra commuter line serves Oak Park?
explain: Oak Park is served by one Metra line, the Union Pacific West Line. It also has two CTA 'L' lines, the Blue and the Green.

q: Before it was renamed in 1964, the Eisenhower Expressway (I-290) was called the what?
explain: On Jan. 10, 1964, the Chicago City Council renamed the Congress Expressway for President Dwight D. Eisenhower.

q: Oak Park's home ZIP codes run from 60301 to 60304. Which nearby ZIP code is NOT one of Oak Park's?
explain: Oak Park's ZIP codes are 60301 to 60304. 60305 belongs to neighboring River Forest.

q: About how big is the Village of Oak Park?
explain: The Village of Oak Park covers 4.7 square miles.

q: According to the Village, about how far is Oak Park from downtown Chicago?
explain: The Village says Oak Park is 9 miles from downtown Chicago, 10 miles from O'Hare and 8 miles from Midway.

q: OPRF's student newspaper, which Ernest Hemingway wrote for, is called what?
explain: The Trapeze was founded in 1912. Hemingway was an early reporter for it from 1913 to 1917.

q: Which OPRF graduate (Class of 1975) is the voice of Homer Simpson?
explain: Dan Castellaneta, OPRF Class of 1975, performed with Second City and is the voice of Homer Simpson.

q: Walter Burley Griffin, OPRF Class of 1896, won the plan for which nation's new capital city?
explain: Architect Walter Burley Griffin (OPRF 1896) won the commission to plan Canberra, Australia's new capital.

q: Before 2002, Gwendolyn Brooks Middle School was a junior high named for which writer?
explain: Emerson Junior High became Gwendolyn Brooks Middle School in Sept. 2002, when a new building opened and 6th grade was added.

q: Hatch Elementary is named for William H. Hatch. Who was he?
explain: William H. Hatch was the district superintendent from 1882 to 1917. Hatch School opened in 1922.

q: The library's Maze Branch is named for Adele H. Maze. Who was she?
explain: Adele H. Maze served south Oak Park as a librarian from 1918 to 1957. The South Branch was renamed for her in 1957.

q: The Dole Branch Library is at 255 Augusta St. Who gave that building to the village in 1939?
explain: In 1939 Mr. and Mrs. Andrew Dole gave the building at Augusta and Cuyler to the village. The branch moved in and took their name in 1940.

q: Oak Park Festival Theatre (founded 1975) performs outdoors each summer in which park?
explain: Founded in 1975, Oak Park Festival Theatre is the Midwest's oldest professional outdoor classical theater. It plays in Austin Gardens.

q: Since 1978, the Oak Park Farmers' Market has been held each Saturday in which parking lot?
explain: The market began in 1976 on North Boulevard. Since 1978 it has been held in the Pilgrim Congregational Church lot at 460 Lake St.

q: 'A Day in Our Village' is held on the first Sunday of June in which park?
explain: A Day in Our Village fills Scoville Park, at Lake St. and Oak Park Ave., on the first Sunday in June.

q: In what year did the Art Deco Lake Theatre on Lake Street open?
explain: The Lake Theatre opened in April 1936 with 'The Ghost Goes West.' Thomas W. Lamb's firm designed it.

q: Since 1937 the Oak Park Art League (founded 1921) has been based in what kind of building?
explain: Since 1937, the Oak Park Art League has been in a carriage house at 720 Chicago Ave. designed by E.E. Roberts.

q: The Oak Park River Forest Museum at 129 Lake St. is in a building first used as what?
explain: The museum opened in 2017 in Cicero Fire House No. 2, built in 1898. The building is older than the village itself.

q: Oak Park's yearly Juneteenth celebration opens with a flag-raising ceremony at which location?
explain: The Village's Juneteenth celebration opens with a flag-raising at Village Hall. The Board voted in 2020 to observe the holiday every June 19.

q: In 2015, Oak Park became Illinois' first municipal what?
explain: In 2015 Oak Park became Illinois' first municipal arboretum and the nation's fourth.

q: Oak Park's oldest known heritage oak, about 280 years old, is which kind of oak?
explain: About 170 heritage oaks remain locally. The oldest known is a bur oak, about 280 years old, on private property.

q: Oak Park has been named a 'Tree City USA' for decades. Which group gives this award?
explain: The Arbor Day Foundation named Oak Park a 2023 Tree City USA. It was the village's 40th year with the honor.

q: Which of these is NOT one of the Oak Park Conservatory's three showrooms?
explain: The Conservatory has three showrooms, the Mediterranean, Tropical and Desert rooms, with more than 3,000 plants in all.

q: In 1970 the Conservatory almost came down. What was proposed to replace it?
explain: In 1970 the Conservatory was nearly torn down for a parking lot for the new Rehm Park pool. Elsie Jacobsen's citizens' committee saved it.

q: About how many plants does the Oak Park Conservatory hold?
explain: The Conservatory's botanical collection has more than 3,000 plants from six continents.
